title: Bound-claim audit (what this project may say)
notes: each row is a sentence plus the check that supports it, re-run at build time; a check that failed is recorded as failed
passing means the code agrees with the sentence, not that the biology is right

claims.sentence: The dosing scheduler is mechanistic: drugs move by a discretised Fickian diffusion PDE and clones compete by Lotka-Volterra dynamics with saturating (EC50) kill kinetics.
claims.limit: The mechanism is mechanistic; the rate constants are declared assumptions, not measurements from this project.
claims.detail: PDE transport (diffusion + Laplacian): True; Lotka-Volterra competition with carrying capacity: True; saturating (Hill/EC50) kill kinetics: True -- the scheduler is mechanistic

claims.sentence: Resistance in this engine is produced by the model, not carried by the initial state: with mutation off and no seeded clone the resistant burden is exactly zero, and with the extinction floor the sensitive population is extinguished exactly rather than lingering as a sub-single-cell density. The engine's qualitative verdict (does continuous MTD control the tumour?) tracks whether a resistant subclone exists at diagnosis, which is an ASSUMED input here, not a measured one.
claims.limit: This verifies the mechanism is doing the work; it says nothing about whether the assumed constants are right, and the verdict's dependence on the pre-existing fraction is a limitation to state, not a result to publish.
claims.detail: mutation off + no seeded clone -> max resistant burden 0.000e+00 (no ghost resistance: True); sensitive population extinguished exactly: True; verdict tracks the assumed pre-existing clone (MTD PFS 172 d seeded vs None unseeded): True

claims.sentence: The scheduling core is not a trained classifier: it solves transport and population dynamics rather than learning a mapping from images to labels. A pretrained protein language model contributes capsid-fitness scoring in the separate design arm, and is labelled as such wherever it is used.
claims.limit: A claim of 'no machine learning anywhere' is false: torch modules and an ESM scorer ship in the design arm.
claims.detail: torch modules present: PositionalEncoding, AAVTropismTransformer, LNPDeliveryMLP, ImmuneEscapeTransformer; esm_inference.py present: False; /api/esm endpoints wired: True -- a claim of 'no black box anywhere' is false as worded

claims.sentence: Runs are stochastic (mutation timing and growth noise) and fully seeded: identical seeds reproduce a trajectory exactly, and results are reported as distributions over replicates.
claims.limit: Reproducible is not the same as deterministic, and neither is the same as correct.
claims.detail: same seed reproduces exactly: True; different seed diverges: True -- the model is stochastic and seeded, not deterministic

claims.sentence: Capsid geometry is the deposited AAV9 structure (PDB 3UX1), assembled with the entry's own REMARK 350 symmetry operators and pinned by SHA-256 verified on every load.
claims.limit: C-alpha trace only: it is not an atomic surface, and it says nothing about conformational ensembles.
claims.detail: PDB file 3UX1.pdb sha256 1a39ed430f8404b9... matches the pin

claims.sentence: The engineered capsid's wild type is VP1 residues 263-736 of that same deposited structure, re-derived from the PDB on every test run.
claims.limit: One deposited model, not a consensus sequence across AAV9 isolates.
claims.detail: 474 residues, derived from the deposit: True

claims.sentence: Every output carries a provenance tier from a fixed vocabulary: ESTABLISHED, EMERGING_HUMAN, ANIMAL_ONLY, PROVEN_FAILED, UNKNOWN -- including permanent PROVEN_FAILED entries for claims this project made and withdrew.
claims.limit: A tier is an assertion about evidence; it is only as good as the citation behind the entry using it.
claims.detail: EvidenceStatus members: ESTABLISHED, EMERGING_HUMAN, ANIMAL_ONLY, PROVEN_FAILED, UNKNOWN

claims.sentence: Rate constants are labelled in the source as CALIBRATED or ASSUMED, with the benchmark measurement that would replace each one identified.
claims.limit: Being labelled is not being measured: every rate is still an assumption until a bench run replaces it.
claims.detail: 7 parameters marked CALIBRATED, 'ASSUMED' section present: True -- the mechanism is mechanistic, the constants are not measurements

claims.sentence: The repository carries an automated test suite covering the physics, the statistics and the refusal paths, with the count computed live and the README's own suite row checked against it rather than maintained by hand.
claims.limit: Tests verify the implementation. They are not evidence about biology.
claims.detail: 1698 test functions in 208 classes across tests/ and danon/multiagent/ (pytest collects more than this wherever a test is parametrised); README defers to this check rather than quoting a count

claims.sentence: A Cox model of clinical covariates reaches C = 0.64 on held-out TCGA-GBM patients, validating the held-out statistical machinery on real data.
claims.limit: That C-index is about age and grade, not about this engine. The engine itself has no estimable patient-level C-index.
claims.detail: engine C-index declared not estimable: True

claims.sentence: The engine is a coarse-grained continuum--agent hybrid, not a discrete cell-by-cell simulation: clinical voxels hold clone densities and drug concentration, so transport is solved on a mesh rather than per cell.
claims.limit: The engine grid is ~4 mm, not the 100 um voxels this pitch originally claimed, and the decimation from a 1 mm scan is a documented lossy step.
claims.detail: engine voxel ~3.67 mm from decimation factors (4, 4, 3) (source 1 mm); ~3667 um, not 100 um; decimation is declared as a lossy step in the module: True

claims.sentence: A 365-day forecast is a sub-second-to-second computation on the engine's phantom (and ~20 s for a full paired case on real geometry), re-measured whenever this audit runs rather than quoted.
claims.limit: Runtime is machine-dependent; the audit prints the machine's own number.
claims.detail: one 365-day arm on the engine's 3178-voxel phantom: 3.12 s on this machine (re-measured at audit time; a full paired case with replicates on real geometry costs ~20 s)

claims.sentence: Molecular inputs are real bulk RNA-seq (GDC open STAR counts), and the pipeline states that single-cell clone fractions cannot be recovered from them.
claims.limit: A claim of scRNA-seq-derived parameters would describe data this pipeline never reads, and `PROVEN_FAILED` in the same module says so.
claims.detail: computational inputs are bulk RNA-seq: True; deriving single-cell clone fractions from bulk is marked PROVEN_FAILED in the module: True -- a pitch claiming scRNA-seq parameters would be describing data this pipeline never reads

claims.sentence: No spatial-agreement (Dice) result is claimed: no reachable glioma imaging collection carries both an expert tumour mask and a second timepoint, so a predicted field cannot be scored against an observed recurrence scan. The refusal is computed from recorded probe counts and flips automatically if such a collection appears.
claims.limit: Absence of a test is not a negative result: nothing here is evidence that the engine's spatial predictions are wrong, only that the public data reachable from this environment cannot test them.
claims.detail: spatial Dice test REFUSED; 5 imaging collection(s) probed, 0 segmentation series, 632 patient(s) checked for a second timepoint

claims.sentence: Drug potency is taken from real measured activity records (ChEMBL) rather than authored: 31 exact glioma-line IC50s for temozolomide, median 135 uM and most potent 6.4 uM, spanning a 496x between-model range, with 19 right-censored records counted separately and their units preserved.
claims.limit: 2D monolayer IC50 at a single timepoint is not 3D tumour kill behind a blood-brain barrier, and the records come from heterogeneous assays whose readout and exposure time are largely unrecorded.
claims.detail: CHEMBL810 IC50: 31 exact of 50 glioma-line record(s), median 134,970 nM, most potent 6,426 nM, 19 right-censored

claims.sentence: The engine's EC50 carries no declared concentration unit, so it is not compared to measured potency: any ratio between them would be unitless. The measured values are reported instead. Declaring a unit would not fix it either, and that is measured rather than argued: the kill law is kill_max * c / (c + EC50), homogeneous of degree 0 in (c, EC50), and the drug transport is linear in its source, so scaling the source strength AND the EC50 by 2^10 (exact in binary floating point) reproduces the 60-day burden arrays bit for bit -- while scaling the EC50 alone moves them, so the measurement is not blind. The engine's concentration scale is therefore a FREE CHOICE, and what the FDA label supplies is a scale, not a potency: from the label's own text, the Cmax at 150 mg/m2 is 7.5 mcg/mL oral and 7.3 mcg/mL IV, the mean elimination half-life is 1.8 hours, and the figure a public-data route usually quotes as a Cmax -- 5.5 -- is the CLEARANCE in L/hr/m2. A unit declaration would make the comparison legal without making the constant measured.
claims.substantiated_by: danon/pharmacology.py::engine_ec50_unit + compare_engine_ec50 (refusal), with the label read and the relabelling experiment recorded by _drug_units_probe.py over outputs_real/drug_units_probe.json
claims.limit: This is a defect, not a feature. Until the engine's concentration scale is declared, its potency constant cannot be anchored to anything measurable, and no calibration claim should be made about it. The relabelling measurement bounds what a unit change can buy: it is a no-op on every trajectory this engine has produced, so the label's numbers cannot calibrate anything by themselves. The label's Cmax is also a PLASMA concentration after a dose in a 70 kg adult -- reaching a tumour kill constant from it needs a blood-brain-barrier and tumour-exposure model this repository does not have, and an IC50 is still not a per-day kill rate. Both blockers survive the relabelling.
claims.detail: engine EC50 unit declared: None; comparison REFUSED -- the engine's EC50 has no declared concentration unit (DrugParams documents only 'conc/day at full-dose vessels'), so an EC50-vs-IC50 ratio would be unitless nonsense. Declare a unit on the engine's concentration scale before comparing; measured values are available (median 134,970 nM, most potent 6,426 nM).; kill law degree-0 homogeneous in (c, EC50): True; scaling source strength AND EC50 by 2^10 reproduces the 60-day burden arrays bit for bit while scaling the EC50 alone does not, so the engine's concentration scale is a free choice; the label's own kinetic scale is a Cmax of 7.5 mcg/mL oral / 7.3 mcg/mL IV at 150 mg/m2 with clearance 5.5 L/hr/m2 and half-life 1.8 h, so what is missing is a MEASURED potency, not a unit

claims.sentence: The wet-lab bridge is built as far as public data allow and then REFUSED on the record. The measured anchors -- 31 exact of 166 ChEMBL glioma-line temozolomide IC50 records with 19 right-censored counted as bounds, and a GDSC2 glioma audit in which 76.0% of IC50s and 34 of 34 temozolomide IC50s sit above the highest concentration tested -- are persisted with the live engine's own constant set, and the artifact states `calibrated: false` with three independent blockers: an IC50 is not a per-day kill rate, the engine's EC50 has no declared concentration unit, and the measured values are largely bounded rather than exact. The artifact carries the four-assay protocol that would close each gap.
claims.limit: This is a measurement of the GAP, not a calibration. The engine's kill_max, EC50 and growth constants remain AUTHORED, and the check fails if the artifact's constants stop matching the live engine's, so the recorded anchor cannot silently describe a different engine. No in-vitro number is substituted into the engine anywhere.
claims.detail: bench anchors persisted in outputs_real/bench_anchors.json: 31 exact of 50 measured glioma-line IC50 record(s) with 19 right-censored counted, GDSC2 temozolomide extrapolations 34/34, EC50 comparison REFUSED, reconciliation calibrated=False, and the artifact's engine constants compare equal to the live engine's.

claims.sentence: Held-out discrimination is reported on an endpoint that keeps its censored patients: the progression cohort is 594 patients with 372 events and 222 censored at last contact, and OS is 595 patients with 491 events and 104 censored. An earlier version of the loader searched follow-up records for a field that only exists on the diagnosis node, so no patient was ever censored and the progression C-index read 0.590 instead of 0.534.
claims.limit: Censoring makes the number smaller and more honest. It is still not clinical validation.
claims.detail: progression endpoint: 594 patients, 372 events, 222 censored at last contact; held-out C = 0.534 +/- 0.053 against 0.539 for age alone -- the multivariable model is beaten by age

claims.sentence: Every covariate proposed for the real cohort is reported with a measured delta-C on the same patients, and Karnofsky status is drawn only from pre-treatment timepoints. A post-treatment KPS is measurably leaky: as a lone predictor it scores C = 0.684 against 0.597 for the pre-treatment value, because it is partly determined by the outcome.
claims.limit: A measured gain of +0.026 inside a fold sd of 0.048 is reported as 'no measurable gain'. MGMT is reachable but caps the cohort at 142 patients, and sub-region segmentation is refused outright.
claims.detail: authored gain figures in the module: none; baseline and post-treatment timepoint sets disjoint: True; post-treatment KPS outranks pre-treatment: True (0.684 vs 0.597) -- a covariate gain is a measurement here, not an estimate

claims.sentence: Diffusion is measured in voxel^2/day, and the bridge to physical units is explicit. The engine's D = 0.35 is 0.35 mm^2/day on the 1 mm phantom but 4.71 mm^2/day on the real 3.67 mm decimated grid -- 13.44x, with `voxel_mm` documented as bookkeeping only, so nothing raised. The spatially heterogeneous transport term is div(D(x) grad C) with harmonic face conductances, which reduces exactly to the engine's scalar D * laplacian(C) on constant D.
claims.limit: The heterogeneous operator is slower or redirected relative to a scalar field of the same mean, never faster: no delivery improvement can be claimed from this change alone. Tissue D values are literature constants and no DTI series is present.
claims.detail: voxel size 3.667 mm from decimation (4, 4, 3) matches realdata's mean convention: True; div(D grad C) reduces to D*lap(C) on constant D: True; the engine's D=0.35 voxel^2/day is 0.35 mm^2/day on the phantom but 4.706 mm^2/day on real geometry (13.44x inflation); 1 voxel^2/day = 1 mm^2/day at 1 mm

claims.sentence: No proposed high-scoring target is reported as a measurement. The spatial Dice target is refused for want of paired imaging with masks; `best_overall_response` is empty for all 617 cases, so no responder label exists and the nearest flag is 4.3% positive and runs backwards against survival; and the in-vitro R^2 is incommensurable because the engine's EC50 has no concentration unit.
claims.limit: Refusing three estimands does not raise the fourth: overall-survival C stays 0.656 and progression C stays 0.534.
claims.detail: `best_overall_response` records: 0 of 617 cases (empty: True); spatial Dice target refused_no_data; in-vitro target refused_incommensurable; no target reports a measured score: True. Reachable response flag: 23 positives in 529 cases, majority-class accuracy 95.65%

claims.sentence: GDSC2's glioma IC50s are largely extrapolations rather than measurements: 76.0% lie above the highest concentration tested, and for temozolomide every one of the 34 glioma values does. The ChEMBL records already in this repository agree independently, with 19 of 50 glioma temozolomide records right-censored.

claims.detail: 8384 glioma rows over 286 drugs and 34 lines: 76.0% of IC50s above the highest concentration tested; temozolomide 34 of 34 extrapolated. An R^2 against these would be a fit to a lower bound

claims.sentence: EGFRvIII is an in-frame deletion of exons 2-7 -- a structural variant -- so it cannot appear in the open Masked Somatic Mutation files. All 1,847 structural-variation files for TCGA-GBM are controlled access, so EGFRvIII status is not obtainable from open data and cannot be a feature of a classifier built here.
claims.limit: Inferring the deletion from RNA-seq junction reads is a legitimate alternative and would be an inference, not a mutation call.
claims.detail: EGFRvIII: 1847 structural-variation files of which 1847 are controlled, against 464 open SNV/indel files that cannot carry an exon 2-7 deletion: reachable from open data = False

claims.sentence: This engine is not reported to predict individual patients: no dataset here pairs baseline tumour state, administered schedule and outcome, and one curve per simulation means a C-index would be 0.5 by construction.
claims.limit: Stating the absence is the honest position; it is not a finding.
claims.detail: engine C-index declared not estimable: True

This is a property of the SIMULATOR, not an accuracy on patients, and is bound to the one-shot re-measurement.

Each stream's constants are declared (KI67_REF=0.15, CLEARANCE_GAMMA=1.0), and stream 4 is an observation, not an input.

claims.sentence: Stream 3 (perfusion) is measured on real cached data: t1ce contrast volumes block-averaged through the segmentations' exact engine transform for 6 BraTS cases (tumour mean enhancement 0.37-0.49), then run PAIRED (same geometry, same seeds) against the null-uniform vasculature: MTD PFS moves by a mean of -1.17 days (sd 1.01, max 3, 18 paired runs; 5/6 cases earlier), steering stays horizon-censored in both geometries (paired delta exactly 0). At engine scale the vessel-source variation contributes about one day. This claim previously ended by asserting that the sanctuary structure 'lives in D(x), which both geometries share' -- a speculation stated as a finding, with no check behind it. It has since been MEASURED: varying D(x) by 3.3x does not restore the difference either (see stream3_diffusion_measured).
claims.limit: A wired-and-measured stream whose measured effect is small is a result, not a failure; t1ce is a vascular proxy, not Ktrans.
claims.detail: cohort 6 cases / 18 paired runs: True; live re-run of 01017 seed 101 reproduces the committed PFS: True (paired delta -3 d; committed mean -1.17 d)

claims.sentence: Stream 3's diffusion arm (D_chemo(x) = D0*(1+2.5*rCBV(x)), the specification's own formula) is implemented against the engine's `diffusion_field` hook and measured on real cached BraTS-2021 cases, PAIRED transport-only: identical mask, proliferation, vessels source and seeds, differing only in the transport field. The mapping produces a 3.35-3.45x contrast in D(x) (1543-2673 perfused voxels per case), and across 3 cases x 2 policies x 3 seeds (18 paired runs) only 1 of 6 policy-arms moves AT ALL: MTD paired deltas -1, 0, 0 days (one seed pair in one case), steering exactly 0 in every case. That is within seed noise at this cohort size -- a 3.4x transport contrast does NOT eliminate a delivery blind spot here, and the effect is of the same order as the vasculature arm. The arm is transport-only by construction because the simulator reduces a supplied field to a mean-one relative pattern, so D0 and the unit conversion cancel exactly and gamma=2.5 is this parameter's only live constant: no absolute diffusivity claim rides on this mapping.
claims.substantiated_by: danon/claims.py::check_stream3_diffusion_is_measured over outputs_real/stream3_diffusion_cohort.json (rebuildable via _stream3_diffusion_cohort.py), field stats re-derived live each audit
claims.limit: The engine arms are the committed measurement, not re-run inside the audit; the field statistics ARE recomputed live. An rCBV map is scalar, so this mapping is isotropic per voxel -- it is not a diffusion tensor, and no anisotropy is fabricated from perfusion.
claims.detail: 3 cases x 2 policies x 3 seeds, paired transport-only: MTD paired PFS delta -1..+0 d (medians +0.0 d), steering +0..+0 d; 1/6 policy-arms move at all; cohort self-consistent: True; case 01017 live field D(x) = 0.35-1.171 mm^2/day (3.3x), 1543 perfused voxels; matches committed arms: True

claims.sentence: Stream 3 consumes MEASURED perfusion, not only a contrast proxy: raw DSC series download from TCIA (UPENN-GBM), `danon.dicomio` reads their JPEG-2000-encapsulated pixels, and `danon.perfusion` integrates the first pass into a relative-CBV map. 3 series are downloaded and measured -- selected as the three smallest by listed FileSize, a rule fixed before any outcome was seen -- across three different acquisitions (TR 1.83-2.0 s, TE 45-51 ms, 700-900 files each). A head-to-tail drift line is subtracted before integration because 30-51% of the raw volume-mean peak on these series is drift, not bolus; without it the first real series called frame 0 the arrival and integrated 45 of 50 frames. The pipeline recovers a planted 3:1 CBV ratio to 0.9% under 0.2% signal noise; on the real maps the transport field spans 15.3-21.6x, and the only endpoint with resolution is the final burden, which differs between transport arms by at most 0.18-8.81% (steering the more sensitive of the two policies). PFS is censored in every arm of this cohort and is reported as censored.
claims.limit: The maps are relative CBV by first-pass integration: no arterial input function is fitted, so this is NOT absolute CBV and NOT Ktrans. The region the engine runs on is rCBV >= 1.5x the map median -- a perfusion-defined ROI, NOT a tumour segmentation, since no segmentation is co-registered to the DSC grid. No result here is about a patient's tumour, and nothing links a series to a survival outcome.
claims.detail: planted 3:1 CBV recovered to 3.009 (0.3% error, 7-frame window); 3 downloaded series: field contrast 15.3-21.6x, final-burden effect up to 8.8%, 6 arm-sets with a censored PFS endpoint

claims.sentence: Stream 4's cohort is counted from the committed CFB-GBM availability manifest (TCIA, DOI 10.7937/v9pn-2f72): 264 patients, 170 with more than one timepoint, and 168 with a usable T1-Gd pair at least 4 weeks apart (393 pairs, 37 of them spanning two scanners). The manifest records that a series EXISTS; the images are not downloaded, so no registration, artefact or comparability check has been performed and no velocity field has been measured. The CFB-GBM collection is not served by the NBIA API this repo probes, so activating the stream requires downloading the collection, not querying it.

claims.detail: CFB-GBM manifest: 264 patients, 170 with >1 timepoint, 168 with a usable t1gd pair (393 pairs, 37 spanning two scanners); images NOT downloaded, so this is availability, not a measurement

It had drifted: the README advertised 31/31 verified while the registry held 33, so the project's own headline number was stale for two commits -- the exact failure mode the registry exists to catch, applied to the registry itself.

claims.sentence: Whether the manifest's cohort could resolve a gain is computed rather than assumed: resampling 168-patient cohorts from the real cached cohort (n=595, overall survival) 24 times moves the held-out C by 0.0219 (1 SE), mean C 0.6429 (age alone 0.6469), with a mean fold sd of 0.0610; the full cohort scores 0.6559 +/- 0.0247. Two consequences follow. (a) Stream 4 is an OBSERVATION -- it calibrates the engine's derived velocity and cannot move a C-index at all until a hazard mapping is declared, so no download of CFB-GBM images would by itself raise the ceiling. (b) At that n any declared mapping would have to clear 0.0219 to be distinguishable from cohort noise, and the covariate effects already measured on the larger cohort (KPS +0.0264, MGMT -0.0006) sit inside the conservative fold yardstick of 0.0610. This measures the resolution of a cohort, not perfusion, fluorescence, Ki-67 or delta-volume.
claims.limit: A design calculation bounds what a study could show; it is not evidence that any stream carries a signal, and the reference cohort is scored on overall survival, which the manifest does not carry.
claims.detail: n=168 (manifest's usable pairs), 24 draws: floor 0.0219 (1 SE) / 0.0610 (fold yardstick); reference cohort re-measured live at C=0.6559 +/- 0.0247 (matches artifact: True); labelled as a design calculation: True

claims.sentence: Stream 4 is implemented as a COMPARISON, not an input: stream4_velocity_agreement reports a measured delta-volume field against the engine's simulated one (rate ratio, Pearson r, sign agreement, peak-growth voxel) and refuses with the census's live counts when either side is absent. Identical fields score r=1.0; a field whose growth sits in a different voxel scores lower, so the statistic can be bad. No measured velocity is ever fed to the engine -- injecting a dR/dt into a model that derives its own would double-count the rate -- and no agreement, however good, can move a discrimination metric.
claims.limit: The comparison has never been run on a real measured pair: 0 are cached, so what a real agreement would score is unknown. This binds what the function IS, not what it would find.
claims.detail: refusal cites the census live (0 cached / 41 retrievable): True; identical fields r=0.9999999999999999, misaligned r=-0.6546536707079771 -> discriminates: True; role labelled a validation target: True

claims.sentence: Streams 1 (5-ALA fluorescence), 2 (whole-slide Ki-67) and 4 (sequential MRI) refuse on their CACHED counts -- no fluorescence captures, no WSIs, zero cached sequential pairs -- while their mappings are implemented and unit-tested, activating when real files are supplied. No stream is back-filled. The census also reports what is RETRIEVABLE without new code, so a refusal is not mistaken for absence: 41 of 630 probed UPENN-GBM patients carry a >=28-day follow-up interval, and the archive carries raw DSC perfusion for 456 patients. (Its 628 patients' worth of CaPTk-processed series are co-registered STRUCTURAL volumes, not rCBV/Ktrans maps: an earlier version of this sentence said perfusion maps, and a downloaded file settled it -- 'AX T1 PRE : Processed_CaPTk', TR 777 ms, one frame per file.)

claims.detail: census: stream1 REFUSED(0), stream2 REFUSED(0), stream3 MEASURABLE(6 t1ce files; archive carries 456 DSC perfusion patients), stream4 REFUSED(0 cached / 41 retrievable pairs)

claims.sentence: Stream 2's measured cellularity reaches the engine's per-voxel density ceiling and is measured there, PAIRED on real cached BraTS-2021 geometry (same mask, proliferation, seeds, policy and initial resistant fraction; the ONLY difference is clones.carrying_capacity). The sweep's endpoints are read from the slide record rather than chosen: its own measured crop extremes over its own pooled density. What it measures is a scale and not a lever. Under continuous MTD the per-seed burden ratio equals the capacity ratio to within a fraction of a percent, so the reported burden is rescaled by K and the tumour's course is unchanged, and PFS does not move. Under the adaptive steering policy the ratio DEPARTS from K, because the engine's switch is gated on ABSOLUTE floors (MIN_VIABLE_DENSITY, DETECTION_BURDEN_DENSITY) that a K rescale does not move with it. So measured packing can matter only where an absolute floor gates a decision, and the ~100%+ burden differences reported at high K are that rescaling, not a treatment effect. An ABSOLUTE cells/mm^3 ceiling is refused: a whole-slide image counts per unit area and the archive's slides record MPP and AppMag with no section thickness to divide by.

claims.sentence: The biopsy stream measures what the archive actually holds and refuses what it does not. TCGA-GBM carries 2,053 whole-slide images at the live GDC count, none of them named as Ki-67 or IHC; the smallest by listed file size (6.01 MB) was downloaded and read -- an Aperio SVS, 9352x4666, MPP 2.0037 um/px, AppMag 5, haematoxylin-only with a brown fraction of 0.0 over the sampled crop. From it danon/histology.py reports 636 nuclei per mm^2 over 4 crops (3,588 nuclei, per-crop spread 460-1579, median nucleus area 76.3 um^2). That is CELLULARITY. Stream 2's mapping needs the Ki-67 labelling index, whose numerator does not exist in this source, so ki67_fraction raises and no r0 is derived: the growth mapping stays unit-tested at KI67_REF=0.15 until a real Ki-67 slide is supplied. The two sources a public-data route names for that numerator were then probed and carry neither: the TCGA-GBM clinical BCR XML (schema 2.7, 108 distinct fields, read back live) has no Ki-67 or MIB-1 field anywhere in it, and Ivy GAP's four public tables (10, 26, 22 and 29 columns) carry no labelling index either -- the one proliferation in the atlas is normalized_area_ctmvp, the area fraction of MICROVASCULAR proliferation, a vessel measurement rather than a Ki-67 index. Substituting a nuclei density for the labelling index would fabricate the growth rate it feeds.
claims.substantiated_by: danon/claims.py::check_stream2_histology_measured_and_ki67_refused over outputs_real/histology_probe.json (rebuildable via _histology_probe.py) and outputs_real/ki67_source_probe.json (rebuildable via _ki67_source_probe.py)
claims.limit: The 636 nuclei/mm^2 is ONE slide, the smallest by listed size -- not a cohort statistic. The zero-Ki-67 finding generalises only as far as the file index plus this one slide's pixels: the index carries barcodes, not markers, so none being named is a lower bound on identifiability, and the remaining 2,052 slides were not downloaded or read. The slide itself is a gitignored cache under data/tcia/ (re-downloadable via _histology_probe.py); the committed record is the evidence, and when the cache is present its size is checked against the record. The stain call is a hue-fraction heuristic, not a validated assay, and the nuclei count comes from connected components in a hue band with an area filter -- clumped nuclei are dropped rather than split, which is part of why crops spread 3.4x. No pathologist count anchors any of it, and nothing here is a grade, a WHO criterion, or a statement about a patient. The external-source probe is a SCHEMA-and-HEADER read, not a pixel read: one TCGA-GBM supplement was downloaded, and the absence of a Ki-67 field is a property of the disease-specific schema (v2.7) it declares rather than of that patient -- but the pathology report PDFs for those same cases are unstructured and were NOT parsed, so a proliferation index typed into one of them would not be visible to this probe. Ivy GAP's gene-level expression table is likewise only read at its header: it exposes gene_symbol and per-structure expression energy, so it does not establish that MKI67 is absent as a transcript, only that no table in the atlas exposes a labelling index. No ivy-named collection appears in TCIA's public collection list (156 collections, read successfully), while per-collection patient and series queries answer with an empty body anonymously -- so 'not in the list' is the strongest statement this machine can make about that cohort's imaging, and the atlas cohort's MRI may still be reachable by other means.

claims.sentence: The spatial solver is verified against exact analytic solutions rather than against itself. The zero-flux Laplacian reproduces its own Neumann eigenvector to a relative residual of 3.43e-14 (float noise), its total vanishes on any closed-domain field to 3.47e-18 relative, the heterogeneous operator collapses onto the homogeneous one at constant D to 2.75e-16, and the observed order of spatial convergence is 1.9944 (second order, measured by halving dx). Its one signed discretization error -- forward Euler integrates clearance at a rate +0.0843%/day high, a direction the scheme cannot avoid -- moves no endpoint by more than 0.7505% in a paired cohort on real geometry, which is 0.0075x that cohort's own seed-to-seed spread of 99.66%.

claims.limit: This is VERIFICATION, not validation: it says the code solves the model it states, not that the model is right about biology. No benchmark against PhysiCell, BioNetGen or FEniCS was run -- the analytic solutions used here are what such a cross-check would compare against anyway, and a matched benchmark problem is a separate pass. The bias is bounded below the model's own stochastic resolution; it is not zero, and it is not corrected, only measured. The paired cohort behind the 0.0075x is ONE case at two policies and three seeds, so it is a bound on this bias, not a general noise model.
claims.detail: Neumann eigenvector residual 3.43e-14; mass identity 3.47e-18 relative; the constant-D branches agree to 2.75e-16; observed spatial order 1.9944 (second); clearance bias +0.0843%/day from the engine's own sub-step rule; over the paired cohort that bias moves an endpoint by at most 0.7505%, against a seed-to-seed spread of 99.66% -- 7.53e-03 of it

The phantom carries 3,178 tumour voxels of 13,824 at 1 mm; the continuous-dose arm reaches progression in every replicate, the switching arm reaches the trial horizon in none, and the paired delta clears the arm's own seed-to-seed spread.

The sample ships homogeneous transport: the heterogeneous D(x) branch is implemented and reachable by a config flag, but costs about 19x per run at this grid, so the default keeps the command to seconds.

claims.sentence: Contrary to the convention that a two-drug calendar should pulse ONE drug against a resistant minority, this measurement alternates the TWO drugs over time. On the same engine, SAME seeds, the alternating arm beats the best single-drug calendar by median AUBC: 0.0433 vs 1.3046 on 30 seeds (ratio 0.0332, dominance advance +150.5 d). The win does not flip across the declared marrow-weight sweep (drug B assumed at 0.3x, 0.5x and 1.0x), and 4 of the 24 declared alternating calendars are inadmissible at every weight while 12 are admissible at the conservative weight. Timed to the label: the screen's boundary lands on the label's own 150 mg/m2 x5d q28d regimen, so 'pulsing one drug' is the marrow-maximum schedule, and an alternation at that maximum makes a resistant population that the single drug cannot.
claims.limit: Measurement on one synthetic GBM phantom, 30 held-out seeds, 365 days. The winning calendar is a combination -- A 150 mg/m2 at 0.3 x full x3d with B 150 mg/m2 at 0.5 x full x3d, no rest -- which at full engine intensity would exceed the marrow budget. Timed to the label and the trial numbers quoted here are the engine's. No patient claim is made; the dosimetry is a synthetic analogue of the label's schedule.
claims.detail: the alternating two-drug calendar is measured by the engine to beat the best single-drug calendar on median AUBC. This row reports the conservative (full-myelosuppressive) drug-B weight only; the full sweep is in the artifact. Simulated on one synthetic phantom, 30 held-out seeds, 365 days; no patient benefit is claimed.

claims.sentence: The alternating win is bracketed by a MEASURED reversal map rather than asserted at one operating point. Re-running the release-1 winner across a declared 40-cell grid -- engine intensity (0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5) on the winner's own levels x pre-existing resistant fraction (0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.3) x growth noise (0.05, 0.2) -- on the same 30 seeds, with the release-1 best single-drug arm RE-RUN at every cell so each cell is a paired comparison (1,440 engine runs), the intensity-1.0 cell reproduces the release-1 median AUBC exactly (0.04332412131403639), no cell reverses the win, and the binding limit is SAFETY, not efficacy: the ANC screen permits at most intensity 1.1 under the conservative drug-B marrow weight and 1.65 at half weight, and the 16 cells at intensity 1.25 and 1.5 fail the floor (modelled nadir 1.24 and 0.59 x10^9/L against 1.5).
claims.limit: The map is a bracketing of the release-1 win, not a validation of the calendar: the window's LOWER edge was never reached (the lowest winning intensity is 0.5 in all eight groups, where PFS already pins to the 365-day horizon), the r0 axis above 0.1 is inert on this phantom (0.1 and 0.3 give identical numbers, which is a property of the initial condition rather than evidence about resistant patients), and every cell is one synthetic phantom under assumed pharmacology constants. An incomplete sweep is refused by the check, and so is a map that found no safety boundary at all.

Measured on one synthetic phantom on the same seeds as release 1; the reversal cells are limits of the claim, not footnotes to it.

claims.sentence: The engine's architecture write-up is committed verbatim and AUDITED against the code rather than trusted. Thirteen declared rules bind it: five statements are REFUTED (a 'deterministic, physics-constrained' engine; AdaptiveDosePolicy described as thresholding on the resistant fraction when it is burden-relative and the threshold controller is CollateralSwitchPolicy; an ANC equation carrying an additive RecoveryRate term the marrow model does not have, since the screen is a reservoir whose budget is DEFINED by the label's own regimen; claims.py described as verifying that the Adaptive policy beat MTD, when its single-drug search returned a null and the measured win came from alternating two drugs; and a two-state ESTABLISHED/PROVEN_FAILED UI flag where the evidence vocabulary has five members). Two are IMPRECISE (mutation written as a multiplicative noise term where the engine draws Poisson(grow_S * mu); BraTS labels sent 'directly' to a spatial carrying capacity where they become a proliferative field) and one is QUALIFIED (a 365-day trial 'in seconds' is ~26 s per 30-seed arm, against 5,388 s for the release-1 comparison stage). Five material omissions are named: the opt-in immune layer (default None), cell motility, the extinction and detection floors, partial cross-resistance (drug_sensitivity_scale_R = 0.25), and the burden-ratio definition of PFS.
claims.limit: The verdicts are DOCUMENT versus CODE, and carry no biological evidence whatever. The document is preserved unedited, so its refuted sentences still read as written: the corrections live in the audit artifact, not in the text. The rule set is finite and matched on literal phrases, so a reworded version of the same error can escape it -- which is why the audited document's SHA-256 is checked, that is, a silent rewrite fails rather than passes. An audit that flagged nothing is refused by the check, and so is an audit whose code-fact snapshot has gone stale.
claims.detail: ARCHITECTURE_EVOTWIN_10X.md audited against the code: 8 statement(s) flagged (5 refuted, 2 imprecise, 1 qualified), 5 material omission(s) named across 13 declared rule(s); document digest and the live code-fact snapshot both match the audited copy. Verdicts are document versus code, and say nothing about whether the engine is right.

claims.sentence: The engine's cell-migration coefficient is a per-VOXEL literal, so it is a different physical diffusivity on every grid, and the consequence is now measured rather than noted. `LEGACY_CELL_MIGRATION_VOXEL2_PER_DAY = 0.02` reads as 0.020 mm^2/day on the 1.0 mm phantom -- where every calibration anchor was set -- and 0.269 mm^2/day on the 3.667 mm real grid, a 13.44x grid factor, against a literature cell-motility range of 0.001-0.005 mm^2/day: above range by 4x on the phantom and 53.8x on the real path, and nothing raises because voxel_mm is bookkeeping rather than a conversion. At 30 seeds on the release-1 winner (whose default arm reproduces the release-1 AUBC 0.04332412131403639 exactly), the winner's own median AUBC moves +5.5% to +10.9% across the declared settings, while median PFS and dominance day are pinned at the horizon in every one of them -- the CONCLUSIONS are robust and the QUOTED NUMBER is not. The single-drug reference arm is where it bites: its AUBC falls from 1.3046 to 0.8175 with motility off, moving the headline winner/single ratio from 0.0332 to 0.0588, so the margin release 1 quotes is motility-dependent by about 1.8x.
claims.limit: This prices the defect, it does not fix it: the engine's default is UNCHANGED, because changing it would invalidate outputs_real/dosing.json (90 minutes of measurement) and outputs_real/release2_sweep.json (24 minutes) and the check fails if the default moves without those being re-run. It is also ONE calendar at ONE operating point on ONE synthetic phantom: the real-grid column is a unit conversion, not a simulation on a 3.667 mm grid, and nothing here decides whether glioma motility should sit at 0.001 or 0.005 mm^2/day. The remedy is to express the coefficient in mm^2/day and convert per voxel size, then re-run both releases.
claims.detail: motility priced: 0.02 voxel^2/day is 0.020 mm^2/day on 1.0 mm phantom voxels and 0.269 mm^2/day on 3.667 mm real voxels (13.44x grid factor) against a literature range of 0.001-0.005; the default arm reproduces the release-1 winner AUBC exactly; winner AUBC moves up to 10.9% and the winner/single ratio moves from 0.0332 to 0.0588 across the declared settings. The engine's default is UNCHANGED, so the release artifacts remain valid and the re-run is an explicit decision.

claims.sentence: Uncertainty is measured rather than asserted, and the label it is NOT is stated first. Propagating the real per-donor MGMT promoter beta distribution (140 TCGA-GBM donors over two probes, mean beta band 0.0119-0.6695) through both arms on a committed BraTS-2021 case gives an interval whose coverage is over (donor, seed) jointly and which is explicitly NOT a Bayesian credible interval -- a posterior needs a likelihood, and this repository holds ZERO engine-output/patient-outcome pairs to build one from (recorded as PROVEN_FAILED so no renderer can call it one). What the decomposition then establishes bounds the 'patient-specific twin' story with numbers: for MTD progression-free survival, re-running the model on the SAME donor moves the answer with an SD of 29.92 days while moving to a different donor's MGMT status moves it 10.38 days -- a repeat run is 2.88x the patient-specific signal, and the input does not clear a 0.05 F test (F = 1.241 on 139/140 df, p = 0.102). The day-365 burden readout DOES resolve it (input fraction 24.6%, p = 0.0016), so which endpoint is read decides whether the patient is visible at all. The arm that looks best is the worst on this axis: the switching policy's PFS is identical for every donor and every seed (365 d, no spread to decompose), and its day-365 burden is not resolvable above the model's own noise at all (MSB 1.80 < MSW 6.99, sigma^2_between <= 0, recorded unclipped).

claims.limit: It is not a credible interval and not a clinical bound. One scalar input is measured here -- MGMT beta, the only engine input in this repository with a real per-donor distribution -- on ONE committed geometry, at ONE trial design (365 days, r0 = 0.01), through a mapping beta -> r0 that is a DECLARED convention rather than a fit, with the engine's rate constants still declared assumptions. So the input channel quantified here is a LOWER bound on the true input uncertainty, and a different anchor moves every number without any code changing. The switching arm's conclusion is about this design: it saturates at the horizon, so another horizon or switch threshold could change it. The F tests ask whether the cohort's beta spread is resolvable THROUGH THE ENGINE, which is a question about the model, not about patients, and the beta of a donor tumour is not the beta of the patient whose case would be simulated.

But the fixed deterministic A/B-alternation reference did slightly better (AUBC 0.0208), while the PPO greedy projection matched MTD (1.2618). This does not demonstrate a PPO-specific advantage or patient benefit.

claims.sentence: Scoring a schedule on a shorter horizon to make the search cheap was measured and rejected. Against the full 365-day ranking, a 120-day screen of the same 20 feasible calendars correlates NEGATIVELY (Spearman -0.588, Kendall tau -0.516): the true 365-day winner is ranked 16th of 20 by the screen and the screen's own pick is 19th at 365 days. None of the top-3 full-horizon calendars survive. Aggressive dosing looks best early and worst late -- which is competitive release showing up in the calibration -- so the search ranks stage 1 on the full horizon and the API returns this verdict to any client asking for a short screen.
claims.limit: Measured on one phantom and one 20-cell grid with 6 seeds; the sign of the correlation is the finding, the exact coefficient is not portable. This says the short screen is unsafe HERE, not that no future calibration could make one safe.

Short screening is therefore NOT used by the search (stage 1 ranks on the full horizon), and the API returns this verdict to any client that asks for one.

claims.sentence: An open-loop dosing calendar is a real input to the real engine: '150 mg/m2 for 5 days then a 21-day holiday' is executed as the policy's day-indexed dose series, pinned against the engine's own recorded dose_A/dose_B arrays. On 30 held-out seeds, pulsing delays resistant dominance by 32 days -- competitive release is real and measurable. But no calendar in the searched grid beat continuous MTD on total tumour burden (best pulsed AUBC 1.3039 vs MTD 1.2741), so the schedule search is reported as a NULL result rather than as a win.
claims.limit: Simulation only, on a synthetic phantom. Pulsing buys time to resistance at the cost of more total tumour. The myelosuppression screen is DECLARED arithmetic on assumed parameters -- not an NCCN, FDA or label threshold, and not measured here. No patient benefit is claimed and none is demonstrated.

Geometry is a synthetic phantom; the safety screen is anchored to the temozolomide label's own ANC threshold and its own 150 mg/m2 x5d q28d regimen, but the kernel shape and drug B's marrow potency are declared choices -- no patient claim is made.

claims.sentence: The engine's fixed uniform grid is measured rather than assumed, and the measurement is not flattering. On a committed BraTS-2021 case (98,447 mm^3 of expert-labelled tumour at 1 mm) the axis-aligned block majority vote the ingestion DOCUMENTS is volume-faithful -- -2.88% at 2 mm, -1.22% at the shipped 3.63 mm grid, Dice 0.9310 against the source occupancy -- while `realdata._decimate_labels` does not produce it: it agrees with that vote at Dice 0.3905 (2,316 differing voxels at the shipped grid), and in single-block probes it sends ZERO of 200 fully-tumour axis-aligned cubes to their own engine voxel, because its reshape groups contiguous runs of source voxels instead of cubes (recorded PROVEN_FAILED, with the six committed engine-ready volumes all carrying the wrong partition and a 1 mm header over 48 mm^3 voxels, understating every physical volume taken from them 48.000x). The alternative block-MAX rule that api_server applies to an oversize upload fails in the other direction: +32.91% tumour volume at the shipped grid, with 34.55% of the vote's tumour added by re-labelling blocks the majority called background. And the discretization moves the OUTCOME by more than the model's own noise: at FIXED physical diffusivity, MTD progression-free survival shifts -32.43% between the 2 mm and 3.63 mm grids, which is 0.79x that cohort's own seed-to-seed spread of 41.23%, while the day-365 spatial burden shifts +43.5% (1.62x the spread) under MTD and +417.6% (7.12x) under the switching arm -- so unlike the clearance scheme's 0.0075x, this artifact is NOT below the model's resolution.

claims.limit: It measures the artifact; it does not remove it. Adaptive refinement does not exist in this repository, so the coarse grid is the last word on spatial detail: anything smaller than a majority block is gone, and the drift measured here is a LOWER bound on what a coarser-but-correct partition would show, because the shipped geometry is currently a different partition of the source rather than a faithful reduction of it. The endpoint compared is a simulated PFS under declared constants, not a patient's, and the drift is reported against the cohort's own seed spread rather than against a clinical margin. The diffusivity is anchored to 1 mm by the constant's own documentation, not by measurement, and on the anisotropic (4, 4, 3) factors no scalar D is simultaneously right along all three axes -- the engine's Laplacian is isotropic in index space, so the mm^2/day figures here are volume-equivalent. The probe samples 200 of the 8,064 blocks; the cohort is ONE case, ONE trial design (365 days, r0 = 0.01) and six seeds; and the arm that drifts most is the switching arm, whose PFS is 365 days for every seed at this design, so its burden drift has no PFS counterpart to check it against.

claims.sentence: Longitudinal walk-forward validation -- run the engine from day 0 and score it against the same patient's follow-up scan -- is implemented and refused, and the refusal is counted rather than asserted. The harness carries 3D Dice, Jaccard, a symmetric 95th-percentile surface distance and the TRUE Jensen-Shannon divergence, which is NOT scipy.spatial.distance.jensenshannon: for the same pair this returns 0.5886 bits while scipy returns 0.6387 = sqrt(0.5886 * ln 2), so a quoted target of 'JSD < 0.15' means 0.15 bits with one and 0.0225 bits with the other. There is nothing to score: the CFB-GBM manifest in this repository declares 393 usable pairs over 168 patients and ships no images, the public NBIA API returns 0 patients and 0 segmentation series for MU-Glioma-Post (203 subjects, 596 post-treatment timepoints, DOI 10.7937/7k9k-3c83) and for Brain-Tumor-Progression, and the GLASS records are now IN this tree rather than absent from it -- while 0 scorable IMAGING pairs remain, because GLASS is genomics and the imaging collections still refuse. GLASS's processed release is a public cBioPortal study (693 samples, 629 sequenced, paired primaries and recurrences) whose mutation records DO carry tumorAltCount/tumorRefCount, so the clonal refusal below rests on the missing MAPPING rule rather than on availability or on a missing frequency. LUMIERE, the one longitudinal GBM collection the NBIA APIs cannot answer for, is re-checked separately because it is real, reachable (Figshare collection 5904905: 91 patients, 638 study dates, 2487 images, 616 expert-rated timepoints) and STILL not scorable: the collection ships its masks as a separate article titled 'MRI data and automated segmentations' (DeepBraTumIA and HD-GLIO-AUTO, two U-Net tools), while its expert contribution is a per-timepoint RANO response class and Macdonald measurements -- NOT a segmentation. A Dice against automated masks is model-versus-model, so caching LUMIERE would not make a Dice measurable, and nothing from it is cached here. What the harness establishes instead is which term moves the predicted tumour at all: the per-voxel growth map sums to exactly 0.0 outside the day-0 mask, so outward movement is the daily motility * laplacian(N) term and nothing else -- with motility forced to 0.0 the share of final burden outside the mask is exactly 0.0, with the engine's default it is 19.35% after 30 days -- and that coefficient is a VOXEL-unit literal, 0.02 voxel^2/day, worth 0.2641 mm^2/day at the engine's real 3.634 mm voxel size, 52.8x the top of the published cell-motility range (0.001-0.005 mm^2/day). A walk-forward Dice measured today would therefore be measuring that coefficient, not invasion.

claims.sentence: Each mechanism this engine carries is ablated one at a time -- same geometry, same seeds, same policy, one parameter moved -- and the effect is reported in units of the model's own seed-to-seed spread, so a term that moves an endpoint less than the noise is not credited with doing anything. On the committed BraTS-2021 case over three seeds and 365 days the load-bearing readouts are: cell motility 5 of 8 (steering day-365 burden 4.628x the spread, MTD PFS 1.233x, the final resistant fraction 113x, dominance day 10.0x), the resistant clone's kill ceiling 3 (burden 1.125x, resistant fraction 1.707x, dominance day 3.0x), the resistance fitness cost 2 (dominance day 2.333x under MTD, steering burden 2.795x), the perfusion-derived transport field 1 (steering burden 1.523x, while MTD PFS moves 0.008x -- nothing), and drug B 1 (steering burden 5172.8x). Two mechanisms move NOTHING above the noise: the mutation term (every readout inert, 0.067x or less) and the asymmetric Lotka-Volterra competition coefficient (every readout inert or unresolved). The control that makes those nulls credible is built into the design: MTDPolicy doses (1.0, 0.0), so ablating drug B under the MTD arm must be exactly zero, and it is -- on every one of the four readouts, in the phantom and in the real case.

claims.limit: Load-bearing is not correct. A wrong coefficient and a right one produce the same positive effect size when the same model is ablated, so this says which parts of THIS model the answer depends on, not that they are the mechanisms a real tumour uses. Inert is not falsified either: a mechanism can be inert because it is wrong or because it is second-order at this design, and the verdict of 'unresolved' (the ratio between 0.1x and 1.0x) is the honest middle that this design cannot settle. The mutation null has a mechanical reason worth stating: with no pre-seeded resistance (r0 = 0) continuous MTD eradicates the tumour to a burden of exactly 0.000 at day 365 for every seed and at both mutation rates, so this model's resistance is its 1% initial condition, not its mutation channel. The endpoints are simulated PFS and burden under declared constants, on ONE case, one trial design and three seeds; and no diffusion-tensor map exists here, so an 'anisotropic tensor PDE' is not what the transport ablation removes -- it removes the spatial variation of a scalar field.

claims.sentence: The accelerated solver is faster by a measured factor and by nothing else: every kernel reproduces its own reference BIT FOR BIT. Removing the Python-level `np.pad` copies and the boolean masks from the two hot operators -- holding the summation order fixed, since float addition is not associative -- buys 1.25x / 2.32x at the engine's own 14x24x24 grid, 1.71x / 3.17x at 64^3 and 2.47x / 3.54x at 256^3 (Laplacian / div-divergence), and a reuse workspace keeps the per-day cost at 1.117x for homogeneous transport and 1.904x when the transport field is heterogeneous. Identity is the gate, not a tolerance: a one-ulp change in a diffusion flux is amplified by 365 iterations of a nonlinear map, so the tests compare whole arrays, whole trajectories and whole replicate batches with exact equality. The two obvious ways to buy the rest do NOT work here and are recorded as measured rather than assumed: batching replicates into one leading array axis is a measured SLOWDOWN (0.833x the serial rate at 16 replicates x 60 days with per-replicate streams, 0.862x with one batched draw -- so it is not the RNG), because an 8,064-voxel field is 64 KB and forty numpy calls on it are dominated by per-call cost; and there is no GPU, no JAX and no CuPy in this environment, so no GPU figure exists to quote. What DOES scale is running the replicates in OS processes, which cannot change a number because each worker runs the unmodified serial engine on its own seeds: 2.080x at 4 workers and 2.006x at 8 on 12 cores, which puts a 10,000-draw 365-day sweep at 1.41-1.46 extrapolated hours instead of 2.94 serial.

claims.limit: These are speedups of THIS engine on THIS machine, not of the problem. The ratios are minima over interleaved repetitions on a shared machine whose own 30-day timing varied 2.7x across 12 consecutive runs, so every figure here is the cost of the work rather than a peak, and none of them transfers to another box. The 256^3 operator numbers are one call each, not a trajectory: no 365-day run at that grid was measured, and the engine's own cases are 8,064-voxel grids, so 256^3 is a scaling probe and not a workload this repository runs. The process ratios are measured at 4 and 8 workers with 16 replicates and do NOT reach the 12-core count, so the extrapolated 10,000-draw figure is arithmetic on a ratio that will not hold on a busy machine, over a grid far smaller than a clinical volume. Batching is a slowdown at these sizes and might not be at much larger ones; that was not measured. Nothing here is a claim about biology, and there is no surrogate model and no rendered frame rate in this repository at all -- those are refused, not estimated.
claims.detail: accelerated kernels are bit-identical to their pinned references on random fields (2 shapes) and over a 30-day phantom run (2 seeds, four field arrays plus both readouts); a warm workspace stops allocating at 2 buffer(s); measured operator speedups 14x24: 1.25x/2.32x, 64x64: 1.71x/3.17x, 256x256: 2.47x/3.54x (laplacian/divergence); day loop 1.117x homogeneous and 1.904x heterogeneous; replicates batched into one array 0.833x -- a SLOWDOWN -- versus 4 worker(s) 2.080x, 8 worker(s) 2.006x

claims.sentence: The five proposed online-only pipelines were bound to data rather than to figure captions. CGGA's clinical releases download without a login and are cached; with the repository's own Cox model -- age, sex and a glioblastoma dummy, fitted once on the cached TCGA cohort (n=595, 491 events, internal held-out C 0.6559 +/- 0.0247) -- applied to CGGA without refitting a coefficient, the transported C-index is 0.7402 on mRNAseq_325's primary gliomas (n=222, 138 events; age alone 0.6600), 0.5763 on its primary GBM subset (n=85, 73 events; age alone 0.5702), and 0.7129 / 0.5821 on mRNAseq_693 (n=403 / n=133). Two of the pitch's numbers do not survive the files: 'n=325 Glioblastoma' is 85 GBM rows inside a 325-row table, and the claimed 0.6412 appears in none of the four subsets -- the mixed-grade figure is higher, which is grade spread rather than overfitting defeated, and the GBM-only figure is age-level. What this does NOT do is validate the engine: it transports a covariate model, no imaging is linked to those rows, and one external cohort at one metric cannot prove 'zero overfitting'. The remaining four pipelines are each refused with the live reason -- the single-cell JSD (no four-state prediction exists anywhere in this repository, and the GEO workbook maps cells to tumours, not states), the in-vitro R^2 (the engine's EC50 has no unit, so the comparison is a type error, and 34 of 34 temozolomide IC50s are extrapolations), the inverse-tensor recovery (there is no inverse estimator, and recovering an injected tensor is self-consistency, not validation), and the BraTS Dice (no probed collection carries an expert mask plus a second timepoint) -- and the GEO archive, the GDSC release and six BraTS cases are recorded as present, so the refusals are about the metric, not availability.
