'Saves lives' and 'an additional year of high-quality life' are refused: clinical_benefit and engine_predicts_patients stay UNKNOWN, and the day-365 readout stays PROVEN_FAILED as a patient prediction, because no dataset here pairs a baseline state, an administered schedule and an outcome. The safety 'guarantee' is a DECLARED screen rather than an interlock: its floor is the temozolomide label's 1.5 x10^9/L, its kernel is fitted to a single label datum, drug-B marrow potency is ASSUMED, and the model's own text says it is not clinical decision support -- and the repository's own sweep records intensities that FAIL that floor (modelled nadir 1.24 and 0.59 x10^9/L), so it constrains a model and guarantees nothing about a patient. The '10,000 schedules in 30 seconds' figure is off by about two orders of magnitude: the measured extrapolation is 1.41-1.46 h on 4-8 workers (2.94 h serial) on the engine's own 8,064-voxel grid, recorded in outputs_real/perf.json. The one real precedent -- the Moffitt phase 2a adaptive-abiraterone study (NCT02415621), which prolonged time to progression at lower cumulative exposure -- is recorded as CONTEXT, not as a result of this engine. The check fails if a shipped surface claims the software saves lives, guarantees safety, adds a year of life, extends a lifespan, or quotes a seconds-scale 10,000-schedule runtime.
claims.substantiated_by: danon/claims.py::check_benefit_safety_and_runtime_are_measured_not_asserted over danon/dosing.py::MyelosuppressionModel + LABEL_ANC_FLOOR, outputs_real/perf.json and danon/outcome_export.py
claims.limit: The precedent is real but it is not this engine: a different cancer, a different drug, a different (non-spatial) model and a phase 2a with a non-randomised comparator, so it supports the hypothesis without transferring any benefit here. A runtime is a property of this machine at this load. And the refusal is the point: code cannot make 'safe for this patient' or 'extends a life' true -- those need prospective trials and regulatory review, not a simulation.
claims.detail: survival claim refused (clinical_benefit UNKNOWN, day-365 PROVEN_FAILED); safety screen is label-anchored and disclaims CDS; 10,000-draw sweep is ~1.4 h measured, not seconds; precedent recorded as context; 163 shipped file(s) scanned for fabricated benefit/safety claims

claims.sentence: A tier a human types is a string; a tier a check derives from evidence is a measurement -- but only if the derivation is SEMANTIC. This repository derives tiers from ingested evidence (DERIVED_TIERS) and enforces that a bundle may RAISE a tier only when it declares an evidence kind, is EXPERT-annotated, is linked to the same patients and passed a unit/bounds check. A file merely EXISTING never qualifies -- the rule LUMIERE makes concrete: reachable, 91 patients, 2487 images, and AUTOMATED masks, so a presence-based upgrade would fabricate a Dice result. The r0 knowledge tier is derived this way and stays UNKNOWN because no ingested Ki-67 labelling index exists. What is deliberately NOT derived is claim_matches_code: the provenance keys are read by the checks themselves, so deriving them from the audit would recurse -- the static-tier / live-support split is load-bearing, not lazy. And a tier is never the audit result: whether a check passes is `supported`, which is orthogonal, and supported claims here carry UNKNOWN and PROVEN_FAILED tiers.
claims.limit: Derivation needs an ARTIFACT, so this changes nothing until a real Ki-67 source is ingested -- it is a trapdoor, not a result. The semantic gate is a policy this repository chose; a different gate could admit evidence this one refuses, and the check states its criteria rather than claiming they are the only defensible ones.
claims.detail: presence-only/automated evidence cannot raise a tier (LUMIERE rule); semantic expert-labelled evidence can; the r0 tier derives to UNKNOWN for want of a Ki-67 numerator; the audit result is never a tier

claims.sentence: A cohort specification handed to a hospital data steward is pinned to the engine, because a steward annex is where a number gets copied into a protocol and never re-checked. Four of the pitch's own claims are contradicted by the code. (1) It maps the necrotic core to K=0, but danon/realdata.py::_label_proliferation weights enhancing 1.00, edema 0.60 and necrosis 0.20 -- necrosis is not zero, and a cohort built to K=0 would encode the wrong label semantics. (2) It quotes a 'documented structural Dice penalty ... 0.3905', but 0.3905 is the DEFECT of the shipped _decimate_labels: the documented axis-aligned block vote agrees with the source occupancy at Dice 0.9310 on the shipped 3.63 mm grid (0.8530 worst case at 7.3 mm), so quoting the defect as documented inverts the record. (3) It attributes '0 scorable pairs' to danon/audit.py, but that count is the claim census, and the longitudinal series is RETRIEVABLE without new code (stream4: 0 cached / 41 retrievable pairs), so the blocker is the cached download plus a mapping rule rather than the absence of data. (4) Its N=30 'above the fold-yardstick noise floor' is computed nowhere here; the repository's own resolvability floor is the fold yardstick (floor_conservative 0.0610), so a size must be justified against that floor. What survives is real: NIfTI intake with the BraTS 1/2/4 label convention, MAX_TOTAL_VOXELS = 4,000,000, a per-patient dosing log the day-by-day engine can initialise (drug, start_day, duration_days, mg/m2), pfs_day with censored patients retained, and expert masks at two timepoints -- and none of it is a guarantee that a cohort exists to be delivered. The check fails if a shipped surface maps necrosis to K=0, calls the 0.3905 defect documented, attributes the census to danon/audit.py, or asserts a powered cohort as N=30.
claims.substantiated_by: danon/claims.py::COHORT_SPECIFICATION + COHORT_SPEC_CORRECTIONS + check_cohort_specification_matches_the_engine_not_the_pitch over danon/imaging.py::MAX_TOTAL_VOXELS, danon/realdata.py::_label_proliferation and outputs_real/grid_artifact.json
claims.limit: Pinning the document to the engine does not make the data arrive: a corrected specification is a request, and a hospital DUA is a negotiation with an IRB that no code performs. A cohort, even a perfect one, is retrospective -- it cannot move clinical_benefit, engine_predicts_patients or the day-365 patient readout, which need prospective trials and regulatory review rather than a dataset.
claims.detail: specification pinned to the engine: voxel cap 4,000,000; tissue weights (1.00, 0.60, 0.20) with necrosis NOT zero; decimation defect 0.3905 vs documented 0.9310 (0.8530 worst case); stream4 0 cached / 41 retrievable; no N is derived here; clinical_benefit and engine_predicts_patients stay UNKNOWN; 163 shipped file(s) scanned for fabricated cohort-spec claims

claims.sentence: The one result in this repository measured in real patients is scored against a baseline under REPEATED patient-level cross-validation, and the two tasks come out differently. From the paired GLASS release -- 1,686 measured mutation rows, 281 patients, 543 specimens, 248 primary-to-recurrence pairs, every allele fraction computed from that specimen's own tumour/reference read counts and none imputed -- danon/evolution_forecast.py scores two tasks at 5 repeats of 5-fold (every patient scored once per repeat by a model that never saw it). Task A, whether a variant the PRIMARY measured is re-detected later, DOES beat its baseline -- and it is scored ROW BY ROW, because a per-patient label is not defined on this cohort: 83 of the 226 patients hold BOTH labels across their own rows, so the first version of this estimator, which read a patient's label off the last row written, was ranking against an accident of row order (122 positives by that rule against 204 by 'a re-detection anywhere', disagreeing on 82 patients). On the repaired unit the pooled out-of-fold AUC is 0.712 over 654 measured rows, with a patient-clustered interval of 0.637-0.788, clear of chance, and 25 of 25 folds above chance; the SECONDARY patient endpoint is AUC 0.648 with an interval of 0.501-0.780, whose lower bound sits 0.001 above chance, so the row-level result is the clear one and the patient-level view is marginal and declared as such. The single seeded split did NOT resolve it (AUC 0.666, interval 0.479-0.832, containing chance), so the earlier UNRESOLVED reading was this cohort's power and not the absence of a signal -- which is why BOTH estimators are kept in the record. Task B, how far a shared variant's fraction moves, does NOT beat persistence: across 25 folds the median advantage is -0.0039 (NEGATIVE -- on a typical fold the model is worse than predicting no change), only 8 of 25 folds beat the floor, and the pooled per-patient advantage 0.0051 carries an interval of -0.0041 to 0.0145 that still contains zero. The single split's +0.0081 advantage was that split's luck. Variants seen only at recurrence are EXCLUDED from task A because a 'gained' variant is re-detected by definition -- an earlier version scored them and reported an inflated AUC 0.85 that was the construction talking. The pairing itself is an INFERENCE and is counted as one: the release declares all 693 of its specimen rows as 'Primary Solid Tumor', so its own sampleType column carries no timepoint and the only signal is the identifier suffix, which nothing here can independently confirm; 1 specimen with an unrecognised suffix is excluded rather than guessed into a fold. Discrimination and calibration are reported as the two separate claims they are: the same pooled out-of-fold ROW probabilities are cut into five equal-count bins of 130-131 rows and compared against the rates they produced, beside a Newton-fitted calibration curve and a Brier score for a constant-prevalence predictor. Measured on the same rows the AUC ranks, the probabilities are calibrated within this package's declared tolerance (slope within 0.35 of 1, intercept within 0.35 of 0, mean within 0.05 of the observed rate): the mean predicted probability 0.728 sits against an observed re-detection rate 0.726, the curve's slope is 0.901 against an ideal 1 and its intercept 0.076 against an ideal 0, and the Brier score 0.1685 beats a constant-prevalence predictor's 0.1988 (skill +0.153) -- so on this cohort the ranking separates AND a probability from this model is a number a reader may hold against a rate. It is one public cohort's calibration and not a general one, and the superseded per-patient pooling had erased that skill entirely (Brier skill -0.036, the value the record published until the unit was fixed). That block is recorded with its bins and its declared tolerances, and the sentence about it is DERIVED from those numbers rather than written by hand, so the two cannot drift apart. The check reloads the cache with the shipping loader, re-runs the single split AND the cross-validation under their recorded seeds, requires the artifact to agree on every metric, asserts that each verdict matches its own interval in BOTH directions, re-derives the pooling block that declares the unit and the label of every pooled score (failing if the pooled scores stop being one per measured row, or if the patients holding both labels stop being reported), asserts the two estimators are both present and actually disagree, fails if the release ever declares real timepoints (which would invalidate the suffix rule), and fails if the therapy, outcome and patient-prediction links ever move off UNKNOWN.
claims.substantiated_by: danon/evolution_forecast.py::calibration_block + danon/claims.py::check_evolution_forecast_is_scored_against_baselines over outputs_real/glass_evolution_forecast.json, outputs_real/glass_variants.json and data/glass_paired/glass_mutations.json, exposed as danon/app_artifacts.py::build_evolution_forecast_artifact and the app's Evolution Forecast screen
claims.limit: Task A's AUC of 0.712 is a MODEST molecular signal on one public retrospective cohort, not a clinical result, and the fact that its probabilities happen to be calibrated here does not make it one: it says a variant's allele fraction in the primary carries some information about whether that locus is seen again, and nothing about what happens to a patient. The panel is a declared 27 genes, not the genome, so a change elsewhere is invisible; there is no purity, no copy number, no therapy record and no outcome joined to these specimens, and years and differing depths separate the two draws, so a change in an allele fraction can come from clonal expansion, sampling, depth or purity and this task cannot say which. The pairing is INFERRED from the specimen identifier because the release declares no timepoint; if that convention is wrong the pairing is wrong and every number here moves. Published allele fractions are a provable LOWER bound on the fraction of tumour cells carrying a variant; a point clone size and an upper bound are refused, and the engine does not consume this channel. Nothing here is a treatment effect, a prognosis or guidance for anyone's care, and clinical_benefit stays UNKNOWN.
claims.detail: re-derived from the cached release with the shipping loader: 1686 measured mutation rows over 281 patients and 543 specimens, 248 paired specimens; both tasks re-run under their recorded seeds and the artifact agrees on every metric. Task A fitted AUC 0.666 (interval 0.479-0.832) against a majority-class 0.661; task B persistence MAE 0.1753 vs fitted 0.1672 with its advantage interval still containing zero. Under repeated patient-level folds the two tasks SEPARATE: task A's pooled out-of-fold ROW AUC 0.712 carries a patient-clustered interval 0.637-0.788 clear of chance, so A resolves; task B's median fold advantage is -0.00391 and its pooled interval still contains zero, so B does not. Discrimination is not calibration, so task A's probabilities were checked against the rates they produced: slope 0.901 against an ideal 1 with the mean predicted 0.728 against an observed 0.726, and a Brier skill of 0.1526 over a constant predictor, so its probabilities carry information a single number does not. Each verdict was asserted to agree with its own interval and its machine-readable resolved-flag, and the timepoint pairing is declared an inference from the identifier rather than a column in the release. One public cohort, a declared 27-gene panel, no therapy or outcome joined: not a treatment effect and not guidance for care.

claims.sentence: A 'clinical execution UI' directive is audited against the engine, not built as written. It asks for four things this repository's own record refuses. (1) Its 'definitive prescription block' -- 150 mg/m2 temozolomide for 5 days -- is the FDA LABEL's own regimen (danon/dosing.py::LABEL_DOSE_MG_M2 = 150, LABEL_ON_DAYS = 5), which is the STANDARD OF CARE the adaptive arm is compared AGAINST, not an output of any optimizer here; and its 'then a 14-day holiday' is a 19-day cycle, contradicting the engine's own 28-day label anchor (LABEL_CYCLE_DAYS = 28, so the label holiday is 23 days). (2) A 'Clinical Mode' that hides 'the explicit algorithmic warnings' removes the basis a non-device CDS tool must display: SAMD_CONTEXT records that a recommendation which DRIVES rather than SUPPORTS a clinician's decision fails the non-device CDS criteria (FD&C Act 520(o)(1)(E)) and is therefore a device, and the frontend's own gate requires MHRA/FDA clearance before any therapeutic use. (3) A 10,000-draw sweep run 'silently the moment the patient's data is ingested' is a measured ~1.4 h on 4-8 workers (outputs_real/perf.json), not a background instant, and running it silently is the opposite of the recorded provenance. (4) 'Exactly how many additional days of progression-free life this schedule mathematically secures for the patient' is a lifespan claim: clinical_benefit and engine_predicts_patients stay UNKNOWN and the day-365 readout stays PROVEN_FAILED as a patient prediction, because code cannot make an 'extends a life' claim true -- that needs prospective trials and regulatory review. The check fails if a shipped surface presents a recommended protocol, a mode that hides the warnings, or a secured days-of-progression-free-survival figure.
claims.substantiated_by: danon/claims.py::CLINICAL_UI_CORRECTIONS + check_clinical_execution_ui_is_audited_not_implemented over danon/dosing.py::LABEL_DOSE_MG_M2 / LABEL_ON_DAYS / LABEL_CYCLE_DAYS, danon/claims.py::SAMD_CONTEXT and outputs_real/perf.json
claims.limit: Auditing the directive does not build the UI, and an honest version would still not make the recommendation safe or life-extending: a surface that drives therapy is a regulated device, and the benefit badge stays UNKNOWN until prospective trials and regulatory review. The regimen the block quotes is real and label-anchored, so it is a true statement about standard care -- it is simply not a personalised prediction, and presenting it as one is the failure this refuses.
claims.detail: directive audited, not built: the 'prescription block' is the label's own 150 mg/m2 x 5 d (28-day cycle, so '5 on / 14 off' is a 19-day cycle), not an optimum; the safety floor is a DECLARED screen that disclaims CDS; the 10,000-draw sweep is ~1.4 h measured, not silent/instant; the 'additional days of progression-free life' figure is refused (clinical_benefit UNKNOWN, day-365 PROVEN_FAILED); the frontend's MHRA/FDA gate stays; 163 shipped file(s) scanned for fabricated clinical-UI claims

claims.sentence: The adaptive-vs-MTD benefit is carried as TWO explicitly different estimands, because they are not interchangeable. The outcome cards call `pfs_extension` the RATIO OF MEDIANS (`median_policy / median_mtd - 1`, a per-case fraction), while the repository's own campaign rule (danon/campaign.py, check S1) describes the PFS extension over PAIRED seeds, reported as a bootstrap 95% interval over replicate pairs rather than as a bare number. danon/paired_extension.py computes the second from the recorded replicates in outputs_real/campaign_log.json -- no engine run, so it is reproducible offline -- and records it beside the first: 18 cases, 54 paired replicates, a paired mean difference of +86.1 d with a bootstrap 95% interval of 73.5-98.4 d, against a median ratio-of-medians extension of 0.388. Every one of the 54 adaptive replicates reached the 365 d horizon, so every difference is a right-censored LOWER BOUND and the interval bounds a bound, never a point estimate. The check fails if the recorded interval no longer re-derives from the log, if it is dropped for a bare number, if the censoring stops being flagged, if the two estimands stop being labelled as distinct, or if a benefit badge moves off UNKNOWN.
claims.limit: A bootstrap interval over paired SIMULATOR replicates is still a simulator result: it does not transfer to glioma patients, and no replicate here is an observed progression. It is computed from a censored endpoint at a fixed 365 d horizon, so it bounds a lower bound -- a longer horizon or an uncensored endpoint would move it, and neither exists in this tree. It is recorded so the number appears only with its method, never because a screen wanted one.
claims.detail: two estimands recorded and labelled distinct: the paired replicate difference in days with a bootstrap 95% interval, and the per-case ratio of medians; interval re-derives from the log on a fixed seed; right-censored lower bound flagged; benefit badges stay UNKNOWN

claims.sentence: A trial-design screen states the counterfactual, shows the noise, and rules out -- and stops there. danon/trial_design.py derives all three from records that already exist: the paired-seed differences in outputs_real/outcome_cards.json (9 cases, 27 paired replicates, policy PFS minus MTD PFS in days, both arms read from the same seeds; the replicates are NESTED rather than independent -- 3 seeds within each of 9 configurations, and those 9 configurations are 3 synthetic initial resistant fractions on each of 3 imaging geometries, so at most 9 independent units stand behind the 27), a resampled interval at each of three scales, and the calendars danon.dosing::MyelosuppressionModel refuses. What it MEASURES, rather than assumes, is that resolvability is a property of the replicate count: the 27 pooled pairs resolve (mean +71.6 d, bootstrap 95% interval 54.1-89.6 d, 23 of 27 pairs separating -- but over at most 9 independent units, never 27), the nine pairs on one image resolve (the marginal one at +4.9 to +35.8 d with four of nine tied), and a single case's three pairs resolve NOTHING -- below the five the repository's own percentile method requires, so it reports unassessed under its own label rather than resolved. The simulated INVERSION day is also measured rather than promised: in all nine recorded cases both arms reach their own switch threshold on the SAME simulated day, so the model shows no delay in that inversion -- the arms diverge after it, in burden. The rule-out is the honest half of a prescription: it names the calendars a DECLARED screen refused -- including the design brief's own '5 on / 14 off' arithmetic, which is a 19-day cycle and is refused, while the label's 5-of-28 cycle is the row the screen's budget is DEFINED by -- and it names no calendar to administer. The check fails if the counterfactual stops re-deriving from the replicates, if a nesting disclosure stops re-deriving from the per-case rows it summarises, if the two unresolved states collapse into one label, if the rule-out is presented as a regulatory boundary, if the inversion-day summary stops matching the per-case days, if the shipped screen carries a fabricated clinical-UI claim, or if a benefit badge moves off UNKNOWN.
claims.substantiated_by: danon/trial_design.py + danon/app_artifacts.py::build_trial_design_artifact + check_trial_design_screen_is_derived_not_prescribed over outputs_real/outcome_cards.json, danon/campaign.py::bootstrap_ci_mean and danon/dosing.py::MyelosuppressionModel
claims.limit: Every number on the screen is a SIMULATOR result over recorded replicates: the endpoint is the model's own RANO >= 25% burden rule, the adaptive arm is censored at the 365 d horizon, and the constants are assumed, so the comparison bounds a model's arithmetic and not a patient's course. The 27 paired replicates are NESTED, not a sample of independent patients: 3 seeds within each of 9 configurations -- 3 synthetic initial resistant fractions on each of 3 imaging geometries -- so at most 9 independent units stand behind the pooled interval, which is therefore narrower than one over independent patients would be. The rule-out is no stronger than the screen behind it: that screen's kernel is fitted to the label's single reported datum, drug B's marrow potency is an assumed weight, and the baseline count is a typical adult reference rather than this patient's -- so a refusal is a statement about the model. And the screen deliberately does NOT do the half that would matter clinically: naming a calendar to administer is a decision this repository cannot support, which is why clinical_benefit and engine_predicts_patients stay UNKNOWN.
claims.detail: the screen states the counterfactual as a statement about the model under declared assumptions, publishes a noise floor that re-derives from the recorded paired replicates (the pooled and per-image scales resolve; every single case falls short of an interval), discloses at every pool that its pairs are NESTED -- the pooled interval resamples 27 pairs over at most 9 independent units, 3 seeds within each of 3 synthetic initial conditions on each of 3 geometries -- and rules out calendars only against the DECLARED ANC screen, the brief's own 19-day arithmetic among them. No calendar is named to administer and the benefit badges stay UNKNOWN; 166 shipped file(s) scanned for a count presented as an independent sample

claims.sentence: The engine can be run CLOSED-loop: an ensemble Kalman analysis corrects its growth parameters and resistant burden at each observation, instead of forecasting from day 0 and stopping. On a synthetic twin -- one seeded engine run as the truth, observations = that truth plus declared noise every 14 days, and an ensemble started from a deliberately wrong prior -- assimilation beat the blind engine on 4 of 4 held-out seeds: mean resistant-burden tracking 94.8% against 83.4% blind, worst seed 93.0%, each scored by the same declared metric over the same days. The check re-runs the held-out twin live and requires the record to match it exactly. The fraction curve is reported as CEILING-SATURATED and is not quoted as a win: under MTD both arms approach 1, so a high fraction score proves nothing.
claims.limit: The truth in this experiment is the engine itself and the observations are that truth plus Gaussian noise, so it validates the CORRECTION METHOD against a known simulated truth -- never the engine against reality. It is not ctDNA data, not a patient cohort, and not evidence that anything here tracks a real tumour: no patient telemetry of any kind is used or bundled, and tracking accuracy on real tumours remains UNKNOWN until prospective longitudinal observations exist. Two earlier versions of this module are recorded as measured failures in the artifact: v1's fraction-only metric saturated, and v2's prior support excluded the truth, so the arm LOST to the blind engine (50.2% vs 63.9%).
claims.detail: re-ran the synthetic twin on the 4 declared held-out seeds: closed-loop assimilation beat the blind engine on 4/4, mean resistant-burden tracking 94.8% vs blind 83.4%, worst seed 93.0%; live summary agrees with the record exactly. The truth is one seeded engine run and the observations are that run plus declared noise -- this measures the correction METHOD, not tracking of any patient's tumour

cannot_establish: that a mechanistic model is more likely to be right than a learned one: mechanism makes a model falsifiable and interpretable, not correct
that any rate constant in this repository is measured: they are calibrated or assumed, and the tiers say which
that passing the audit means a judge should believe the biology: the audit checks the code against its own sentences
that the engine predicts a patient's course, or that any schedule here extends a life -- both require prospective trials
